Container.Name: Tezca
Container.Overview: Tezca is a self-hosted sync server for Obsidian: live, end-to-end encrypted sync between your devices, and shared folders you can edit together in real time. The server only ever stores encrypted data.[br][br]Set Public URL to the address your devices will use (Obsidian on phones needs HTTPS, so put it behind a reverse proxy such as Nginx Proxy Manager, or use Tailscale). After the first start, open the WebUI to see how to claim the server: the claim link is in the container's log. Install the Tezca plugin in Obsidian with BRAT (alexjsp/tezca-obsidian-sync).
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: obsidian sync notes markdown e2ee encrypted collaboration self-hosted livesync
Container.Changes: ### 0.4.0 - Recovery key, offline recovery script, longer edit history and many fixes. ### 0.3.3 - First Unraid template. Runs as nobody:users (PUID 99 / PGID 100) with data in /mnt/user/appdata/tezca.
Container.Requires: A domain name with HTTPS (for example through Nginx Proxy Manager, Cloudflare Tunnel or Tailscale) if you want to sync phones and tablets.

Config.Name: WebUI / sync port
Config.Description: Port the server listens on. Point your reverse proxy here (WebSockets on /ws must be allowed).

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database and (encrypted) attachments. Back this folder up.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: The address your devices use to reach this server, e.g. https://notes.example.com. It goes into claim and invite links.

Config.Name: Server name
Config.Description: Shown on the server's web pages and in invites.

Config.Name: Largest attachment (MB)
Config.Description: Files bigger than this don't sync. If you use a reverse proxy, allow request bodies a little bigger than this.

Config.Name: Guest storage (MB)
Config.Description: How much storage (attachments and note edits) each guest (someone who joined a shared folder without an account here) may use. 0 = unlimited.

Config.Name: History (days)
Config.Description: How long note history (versions and the edit log) is kept.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User the server runs as (it owns the data folder). 99 = nobody.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group the server runs as. 100 = users.
